title: Microservices
concept: Building microservices with XIOM — small, focused services communicating over HTTP/gRPC with observability, resilience, and deployment patterns.
why: Monoliths don't scale organizationally. Microservices decompose problems into independent, deployable units — each written in the best language for the job.
tips: Each microservice should own its data — no shared databases between services
Circuit breakers prevent cascading failures — a slow downstream shouldn't take down upstream
Observability is NOT optional in microservices — you can't debug what you can't see
Start with a monolith, extract microservices when the pain of the monolith exceeds the cost of distribution
common_mistakes: Microservices before product-market fit — premature distribution adds complexity, not value
Shared databases between services — creates tight coupling that defeats the purpose
No health checks or monitoring — distributed systems fail in unpredictable ways
